title: unify auth header semantics, add scoped tokens and request-signing for openai-compat
author: Maya Patel
description:
Motivation: The OpenAI-compat layer has historically accepted a mix of Authorization header shapes (Bearer <key>, Redwood-Key: <key>, and project-scoped headers) which produced inconsistent behavior for scoped tokens and streaming websocket upgrades. This PR standardizes header semantics across the API surface (REST, streaming, and websocket upgrades), introduces scoped tokens for project/org scoping, and implements lightweight request signing with nonce headers to mitigate replay attacks for sensitive operations.

Summary of changes: consolidated auth parsing into packages/openai-compat/src/auth.ts; introduce scoped-token parsing and enforcement; add request-signing middleware that validates X-Request-Nonce + X-Signature HMAC-SHA256 for high-risk endpoints (tool/function-calling, model upload, admin routes); update CORS preflight to expose new headers (X-Request-Nonce, X-Signature, X-Project-ID) and increase preflight cache for common clients; wiring for streaming endpoints and websocket upgrader to accept ephemeral scoped tokens and validate signatures on initial handshake; test and docs updates.

Behavioral contract (externally visible):
- Authorization header still accepts Bearer and Redwood-Key for backward compatibility.
- New header X-Project-ID may be sent to route requests within org-scoped tokens; if absent and token is project-scoped the project is inferred from token payload.
- Scoped tokens carry claims of the form: scope=project:<project-id>:roles=<comma-separated-roles>; enforcement is checked per-route (serve/generate, tools.invoke, admin).
- Streaming and websocket upgrade flows require the same signature checks as REST for operations that change state (tool calls, uploads). Non-state streaming (pure text generation) skips signature requirement but still supports scoped tokens.
- CORS policy now exposes X-Request-Nonce, X-Signature, X-Project-ID and caches OPTIONS for 600s.

Checklist: 
- [x] unify header parsing and normalization
- [x] implement scoped-token format and enforcement stubs
- [x] add request-signing middleware (nonce validation + HMAC check)
- [x] extend streaming/ws auth paths to use new middleware
- [x] update openai-compat shim to translate existing Authorization shapes to normalized internal auth context
- [x] tests for walker (unit) and an integration test that covers streaming + tool-call handshake
- [x] update docs and changelog snippets

Testing and CI: initial push failed lint (missing docstring in auth util) and a flaky streaming test. Fixed by adding a clarifying doc, bumping a 200ms timeout in the integration harness, and pinning a test seed. CI then passed all suites including e2e-streaming.

Rollout / compatibility: This change is backwards-compatible for existing API keys and most clients. Scoped tokens and signature enforcement are opt-in per-route via feature flags controlled in the config (default: signatures off for non-admin routes). The openai-compat layer will log a deprecation notice when clients use legacy Redwood-Key without project scoping to encourage migration.

Notes for reviewers: focus on the auth parsing normalization and websocket handshake validation; verify we don't accidentally require signatures for every streaming generate call (only stateful flows). The scoped-token parser is intentionally conservative; we only validate route-level permissions and leave further claim checks to downstream RBAC middleware.

Related: ENG-9382 (design notes in Linear), SEC-127 (threat modeling), small follow-up will add UI for token minting and rotate nonces in the dedicated proxy.
commits: unify(auth): centralize header parsing and normalize incoming keys
feat(auth): scoped token parser and enforcement stubs
fix(tests): stabilize streaming handshake test; increase timeout
docs: openai-compat auth header docs and upgrade notes
review_comments: Liam O'Connor: Please confirm the websocket upgrade path still accepts query-string tokens for legacy clients. If not, add a compatibility shim.
Maya Patel: Added compatibility shim that translates query-token to Authorization header on initial handshake. Documented in docs/openai_compat_auth.md.
Diego Ramirez: The nonce store needs a TTL / eviction policy to avoid unbounded growth. Can we use the existing redis rate-limiter bucket?
Maya Patel: Wired nonce store to redis with 5 minute TTL; fallback to in-memory LRU in dev mode. Added tests for TTL semantics.
Sana Gupta: Recommend exposing X-Project-ID only for accepted CORS origins to avoid leaking project IDs to arbitrary origins.
Maya Patel: Restrict exposed headers to configured allowlist and added a note in the changelog about default origin restrictions.
Diego Ramirez: Approving after small nits fixed (docstring and a null-check on token parsing).
ci_history: initial: lint fail -> fix docstring; integration: streaming test flaky -> bumped timeout; final: all checks pass
release_notes: Standardize API auth headers; introduce scoped tokens for project-level scoping; optional request-signing (X-Request-Nonce + X-Signature) for stateful endpoints; CORS updated to expose new auth headers. Backwards compatible by default; opt-in signing per-route via feature flag.
notes: This PR is the backend half of a two-part migration. A follow-up will add CLI/token-minting UI and rotation guidance for customers on Dedicated/Private deployments.
proof_of_concept: e2e integration test included: streaming-handshake.spec.ts simulates an ephemeral project-scoped token + nonce signature on upgrade and asserts the tool-call invocation flow succeeds.
